mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening demand environment, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last month signals a strengthening supply environment, which leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a tight labor market and wage inflation, which leads to increased costs and reduced corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure and monetary tightening, which leads to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand environment, which leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST has increased for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average and the GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter, it signals a robust supply environment and economic growth, which leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA and GDPC1 increases > 1% QoQ
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO > 12-month MA and GDPC1 increased by more than 1% QoQ.
